content.intro: Learn template escaping and safe output through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Template Escaping and Safe Output matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines template escaping and safe output as part of django templates and dynamic pages. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Automatic HTML escaping; Safe-string concepts; Why unrestricted safe output is dangerous; Preventing cross-site scripting; Rendering user-generated content appropriately. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Automatic HTML escaping
items.text: Django templates autoescape ordinary variable output by default. Marking untrusted content as safe bypasses that protection and can create XSS risk; output encoding is context-specific.

items.title: Safe-string concepts
items.text: Safe-string concepts is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Why unrestricted safe output is dangerous
items.text: Why unrestricted safe output is dangerous is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Preventing cross-site scripting
items.text: XSS happens when attacker-controlled content is executed in a browser context. Keep template escaping enabled, validate context-specific output, and avoid unsafe HTML construction.

items.title: Rendering user-generated content appropriately
items.text: For Rendering user-generated content appropriately, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

content_blocks.troubleshooting: Avoid the safe filter for untrusted content; escaping does not replace URL validation, authorization, or a content policy.
